did_you_know.text: Did you know? The psalm opens with the heading “For the music director, with stringed instruments; a psalm, a song,” indicating that it was intended for musical performance.
Did you know? The psalm begins with three consecutive requests: for grace, blessing, and God’s shining presence—“May he be gracious to us and bless us; may he shine his face upon us.”
Did you know? The purpose of the blessing is not merely personal: the psalmist asks that God’s way be known throughout the earth and that his salvation be revealed among all nations.
Did you know? The verse repeats the call “May the peoples praise you” twice, emphasizing that all nations are called to give thanks to God.
Did you know? The joy of the nations is connected to just judgment and guidance: they rejoice because God judges the peoples fairly and guides them on earth.
Did you know? The blessing of the land is described in simple, concrete terms: “The earth has yielded its produce”—the land produces its harvest.
Did you know? The psalm’s conclusion connects God’s blessing with reverence for God throughout the world: “May God bless us, and may all the ends of the earth fear him.”
